s: A company has an organization in AWS Organizations that includes a separate AWS account for each of the company's departments. Application teams from different departments develop and deploy solutions independently. The company wants to reduce compute costs and manage costs appropriately across departments. The company also wants to improve visibility into billing for individual departments. The company does not want to lose operational flexibility when the company selects compute resources. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Use AWS Budgets for each department. Use Tag Editor to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans.

Configure AWS Organizations to use consolidated billing. Implement a tagging strategy that identifies departments. Use SCPs to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans.

Configure AWS Organizations to use consolidated billing. Implement a tagging strategy that identifies departments. Use Tag Editor to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase Compute Savings Plans.
Use AWS Budgets for each department. Use SCPs to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase Compute Savings Plans.

w.y: Consolidated billing gives one bill with per-account visibility and shared discounts. Department tags, applied with Tag Editor and activated as cost allocation tags, add finer attribution. Compute Savings Plans reduce cost while keeping flexibility across instance family, size, Region, OS, and even Fargate and Lambda. That preserves the freedom to choose compute resources.

o.A: Budgets only alert on spend, and EC2 Instance Savings Plans lock you to one instance family in one Region, reducing flexibility.
o.B: SCPs restrict permissions and cannot apply tags, and EC2 Instance Savings Plans reduce flexibility.
o.C: Correct: consolidated billing, a tagging strategy applied with Tag Editor, and flexible Compute Savings Plans meet every requirement.
o.D: SCPs cannot apply tags, and Budgets alone does not provide consolidated billing visibility.
